prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Context: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) NextGen/National Airspace System (NAS); National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Airspace Technology Demonstrations 3 (ATD-3). Actors: FAA traffic managers/controllers, airline air traffic control (ATC) coordinators/dispatchers, aircraft/operators/pilots/crews, American Airlines, public/industry/air traffic management (ATM) stakeholders. Aircraft aids: flight management systems, onboard weather radar. Traffic Management Initiatives (TMIs) divert/meter; managers designate Flow Constrained Areas (FCAs). Severe Weather Avoidance Plans (SWAP)=Playbook routes, 2–8-hour horizon. Dispatchers must file ≥45 minutes pre-pushback. Collaborative Trajectory Options Program (CTOP) receives operator route/delay preferences; no postdeparture optimization. Crews coordinate alternatives with controllers/dispatchers; conflict avoidance requires controller coordination. NASA Dynamic Weather Routes (DWR), extending Direct-To, continuously analyzes flights ≥10,000 ft using tracks/plans/weather/airspace/traffic. Maneuver Start Point (MSP): adjustable coordination delay, default five minutes, or predicted high-altitude entry (Fort Worth Center=ZFW: FL240); initializes advisories, snaps to flight-plan fix within 10 nmi. Return Capture Fix (RCF): last fix inside limit rectangle (~200 nmi beyond ZFW), or before Standard Terminal Arrival Route (STAR). Historical direct-clearance polygons retain logic in Future ATM Concept Evaluation Tool (FACET)/National Airspace System Constraint Evaluation and Notification Tool (NASCENT); city-pair selection possible. Wind-corrected MSP–RCF savings must meet user minimum (default five minutes). Weather/optional-traffic avoidance inserts one/two minimum-delay auxiliary waypoints, fix-radial-distance format; optional named-fix snapping. Both trajectories congestion/Special Use Airspace (SUA)-checked; polygon avoidance handles nonweather obstacles. Trial edits update savings/conflicts within one second; warnings precede clearance requests/issuance. DWR sends qualifying advisories to responsible manager/coordinator’s prominent, savings-ordered flight list; retains flights qualifying at latest update. Entries: flight ID/call sign, savings, city pair, aircraft type, RCF/waypoint count, restrictions/conflicts. Indicators: traffic (TR)=minutes-to-conflict; sector load (SC)=yellow/red congestion; weather (WX); R=active Route TMI. Users select/modify before clearance.

New part:
U0104: The proposed ‘DWR’ advisory is shown as a dashed-white line.
U0105: The downstream ‘Capture fix’ used to compute the direct route, and the ‘Auxiliary waypoint’ used to find the route around convective weather polygons, are displayed as well.
U0106: Flights that have sufficient user-defined flight-time savings are displayed in the ‘DWR list’ on the top-left part of the big window.
U0107: Figure 5: DWR Route Display Auxiliary Waypoint Return Capture Fix Maneuver Start (SWAP Route) Point (MSP) The long window at the bottom shows the current flight plan route and DWR advisory, along with time- savings for various downstream fixes at left.
U0108: This is labeled as the ‘Capture fix menu & flying time savings’ in the figure.
U0109: The two windows on the right show the sector congestion for the current flight plan route (top) and the DWR advisory (bottom).
U0110: The corresponding sector congestion values (as red or yellow sectors) for those routes are shown within.
U0111: Red sectors are those where the congestion is caused by aircraft that are all currently airborne, while yellow sectors have proposed departure aircraft causing predicted congestion.
U0112: This allows DWR users to visualize proposed routes and modify them if necessary using point, click, and drag inputs.
U0113: Users can adjust the RCF, the number and position of auxiliary waypoints, and the MSP through interactive points, click, and drag actions if needed.
U0114: Metrics, including flight time savings (or delay), proximity to current and forecast weather, downstream sector congestion, traffic conflicts, and SUA conflicts, all update dynamically as the user modifies a proposed route.
U0115: Conflicts with weather or traffic cause DWR to dismiss a potential reroute (trial plan) and keep searching for another (see Figure 6).
U0116: Figure 6: Example of trial plan with weather and traffic conflicts that would prevent DWR from suggesting this route.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
